title: finding(gate): the expression-carriage census's dialect blind spot is itself blind to JS object-literal node blocks — and prints "✅ Dialect blind spot: none" anyway
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) on behalf of the objectui#8140 finisher, which measured it while fixing a red on PR #8324 but had no standing to widen its own scope. ⛔ Not claimed.

**Observation-class, not a live defect.** Nothing is escaping the gate *today*. The finding is that the mechanism which is supposed to tell us when something starts escaping cannot see this whole class, while the summary line reads as full coverage.

## What was measured

`scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` publishes two things: the judged population, and a blind-spot measurement that is meant to catch fences the census is not judging. That second measurement is `unscannedJsonLike` (`scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs:666-673`), and it only counts a fence when **`fence.ok`** — i.e. when the body *parses as JSON*.

That is the gap. A fence can author a real node tree and still not parse as JSON.

Measured across `content/docs/components`, the fence population splits:

| tag | total | JSON-ish body | TS `interface` body | other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ```plaintext | 80 | 6 | 71 | 3 |
| ```json | 4 | 4 | — | — |

Of those six plaintext JSON-ish blocks, one was PR #8324's (strict JSON, double-quoted keys — it *did* parse, so `unscannedJsonLike` caught it, which is how the red surfaced). **The other five are JavaScript object literals** — unquoted keys, single-quoted strings:

- `content/docs/components/complex/filter-ui.mdx:10`
- `content/docs/components/complex/sort-ui.mdx:10`
- `content/docs/components/complex/view-switcher.mdx:10`
- `content/docs/components/feedback/toaster.mdx:39`
- `content/docs/components/navigation/header-bar.mdx:83`

Every one authors a real node tree. None parses as JSON, so none is `fence.ok`, so none is counted by `unscannedJsonLike` — and none is in the judged population either. They sit in **neither**, while the script prints:

```
✅ Dialect blind spot: none
```

## Why it matters, and why it is not urgent

The class objectui#7851 exists to catch is an expression on a typed node riding an uncarried channel. Written in the object-literal style above, such a block would be invisible to both the census and its own blind-spot check — the detection mechanism reports full coverage precisely where it has none.

It is not urgent because the corpus is currently clean: `grep -c '${'` returns **0** in all five files. The lit control on the same instrument fires (151 `${` occurrences across `content/docs`), so that zero is a real zero and not a broken query.

## ⚠️ The wrong fix

Adding `plaintext` to `JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES`. That was considered and rejected on PR #8324 by content: `plaintext` is not a JSON dialect, and admitting it would let *every* future JSON-in-plaintext block through unjudged — the exact blind spot this gate closes. The five blocks above are the proof, not the counterexample: they are why the census never counted them.

## Fix shape (for triage, not ruled)

- **A — widen what counts as "JSON-like" for the blind-spot measurement only.** Detect a body that is a node tree without requiring strict-JSON parse (an object literal whose first key is `type`, say), and report it as unscanned. The judged population is unchanged; only the honesty of the coverage line improves.
- **B — retag the five blocks.** Convert them to strict JSON and fence them ```json, putting them in the judged population. Larger diff, touches five pages' teaching content, and each block would need to still read well as an example.
- **C — declare them.** A shrink-only exemption list naming the five, so the coverage line can stay `none` truthfully and the population is closed against a sixth.

⛔ The wrong answer in any direction is leaving the summary line saying `none` while the measurement behind it cannot see this class.

## Related

objectui#7851 (the class the census exists to detect) · PR #8324 (where this was measured) · objectui#7896 / objectui#8115 (neighbouring docs-gate census findings, neither covering this)

## Dedup

`search_issues` over open issues for `expression-carriage` / `JSON_FENCE_LANGUAGES` / `"dialect blind spot"` — 28 hits, top 10 read. Nearest: #7896, #7966, #8115, #8047 — all docs/gate census findings, none naming `unscannedJsonLike` or the object-literal class. ⚠️ The reporting dev ran **no** dedup search; this one is the PM's and is bounded to open issues.
